title: Towards Open Set Deep Networks
authors: A. Bendale; T. E. Boult
method: OpenMax (Weibull EVT on penultimate activations)
main_contribution: First deep open-set framework replacing softmax with OpenMax
difference_from_our_proposal: Generic benchmark; ignores agricultural domain shift post-harvest conditions and asymmetric food-safety risks

title: A Baseline for Detecting Misclassified and Out-of-Distribution Examples in Neural Networks
authors: D. Hendrycks; K. Gimpel
method: Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP)
main_contribution: Foundational baseline showing softmax probabilities detect OOD
difference_from_our_proposal: Overconfident on far OOD; does not address fine-grained post-harvest condition shifts or selective risk-coverage curves

title: Enhancing The Reliability of Out-of-distribution Image Detection in Neural Networks
authors: S. Liang; Y. Li; R. Srikant
method: ODIN (Temperature scaling + input perturbation)
main_contribution: Separates ID and OOD using large temperature scaling and input noise
difference_from_our_proposal: Requires test-time backpropagation and validation OOD tuning; untested on agricultural domain shifts

title: A Simple Unified Framework for Detecting Out-of-Distribution Samples and Adversarial Attacks
authors: K. Lee; K. Lee; H. Lee; J. Shin
method: Mahalanobis distance on intermediate feature representations
main_contribution: Models class-conditional Gaussian distributions in feature space
difference_from_our_proposal: High covariance inversion complexity; tested only on synthetic OOD benchmarks without agricultural shift

title: Energy-based Out-of-distribution Detection
authors: W. Liu; X. Wang; J. Owens; Y. Li
method: Negative log-sum-exp free energy scoring
main_contribution: Proves free energy aligns with input log-marginal density better than softmax
difference_from_our_proposal: Focuses on general natural images; does not integrate asymmetric food-hazard penalties or selective fresh/rotten sorting

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
authors: Y. Geifman; R. El-Yaniv
method: Selective risk-coverage optimization via Softmax Response
main_contribution: Formalized deep selective classification with guaranteed error bounds
difference_from_our_proposal: Assumes closed-set inputs; fails when confronted with open-set anomalies or unseen chemical adulterants

title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
authors: Y. Geifman; R. El-Yaniv
method: Three-headed architecture (classification selection auxiliary)
main_contribution: End-to-end learned rejection head for selective prediction
difference_from_our_proposal: Requires complete re-training of backbones; assumes closed distribution without external cross-dataset domain shifts

title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
authors: C. Guo; G. Pleiss; Y. Sun; K. Q. Weinberger
method: Post-hoc Temperature Scaling
main_contribution: Popularized single-parameter temperature scaling to minimize ECE
difference_from_our_proposal: Focuses solely on closed-set calibration; does not detect or reject OOD or open-set instances

title: Open-Set Recognition: a Good Closed-Set Classifier is All You Need?
authors: S. Vaze; K. Han; A. Vedaldi; A. Zisserman
method: Maximum Logit Score (MLS) on well-regularized backbones
main_contribution: Proved closed-set training quality correlates strongly with OSR performance
difference_from_our_proposal: Evaluated on curated fine-grained benchmarks; does not explore post-harvest degradation or chemical adulteration

title: Generalized Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Survey
authors: J. Yang; K. Zhou; Y. Li; Z. Liu
method: Taxonomic framework for anomaly novelty and OOD detection
dataset: Survey analysis across standard ML benchmarks
main_contribution: Synthesized mathematical relationships between OSR OOD and selective prediction
difference_from_our_proposal: Comprehensive survey paper without empirical evaluation on agricultural or food safety datasets

title: Known and unknown class recognition on plant species and diseases
authors: Y. Meng; M. Xu; H. Kim; S. Yoon; Y. Jeong; D. S. Park
method: Distance-based feature manifold thresholding
main_contribution: Demonstrated open-set recognition on plant leaf diseases to reject unseen pathogens
difference_from_our_proposal: Evaluates foliar leaf diseases under lab backgrounds; does not study edible fruits or chemical preservation

title: Open-Set Recognition for Potato Leaf Disease Identification Using OpenMax
authors: I. Verawati; M. Hisam; Y. Pristyanto
method: Xception backbone coupled with OpenMax
main_contribution: Applied EVT-based OpenMax to agricultural crop disease identification
difference_from_our_proposal: Single-crop foliar leaf study; does not address multi-fruit sorting cross-dataset shifts or chemical adulteration

title: Deep Learning-based Open Set Domain Adaptation for Plant Disease Recognition across Multiple Greenhouse Scenarios
authors: A. Fuentes; S. Yoon; J. Lee; T. Kim; D. S. Park
method: Open-Set Domain Adaptation with adversarial alignment
dataset: Greenhouse tomato and pepper leaf disease dataset
main_contribution: Addressed open-set recognition coupled with covariate greenhouse domain shift
difference_from_our_proposal: Focuses on greenhouse leaf pathogen adaptation; does not inspect edible fruit freshness cold storage or food adulterants

title: Plant Disease Recognition Datasets in the Age of Deep Learning: Challenges and Opportunities
authors: M. Xu; J.-E. Park; J. Lee; J. Yang; S. Yoon
method: Meta-review of dataset biases and open-world challenges
main_contribution: Critiqued lack of open-set and cross-dataset validation in existing plant AI
difference_from_our_proposal: Methodological survey; does not provide an experimental framework or evaluate post-harvest fruit adulteration

title: FruitVision: A benchmark dataset for fresh rotten and formalin-mixed fruit detection
authors: M. H. I. Bijoy; S. Z. Tasnim; S. A. Awsaf; M. Z. Hasan
method: Standard closed-set CNN baselines (VGG ResNet MobileNet)
main_contribution: First large open-access benchmark explicitly including formalin-treated fruits
difference_from_our_proposal: Uses naive closed-set training where formalin is an explicit target; does not test open-set rejection

title: Computer vision based deep learning approach for toxic and harmful substances detection in fruits
authors: A. Sattar; M. A. M. Ridoy; A. K. Saha; H. M. H. Babu; M. N. Huda
method: DurbeenNet (custom CNN with dilated convolutions)
main_contribution: Proposed specialized architecture for closed-set toxic substance identification
difference_from_our_proposal: Purely closed-set binary classifier; evaluated on random splits with severe background leakage risk; no OOD rejection

title: Simulated Annealing and CoAtNet-based Explainable AI Framework for Fruit Quality and Freshness Classification
authors: S. Saranya; D. Dhanya; S. Srinivasan; P. Joseph
method: CoAtNet + Simulated Annealing + Grad-CAM XAI
dataset: Multi-fruit dataset with fresh rotten formalin-mixed samples
main_contribution: Combined CNN-Transformer with heuristic meta-optimization for fruit grading
difference_from_our_proposal: Closed-set multi-class formulation; over-parameterized model claiming 99.6% accuracy without OOD validation

title: ToxiFruit: A Multi-Class Image Dataset for Formalin Adulteration Detection in Fruits
authors: A. Sattar; M. A. M. Ridoy; M. H. Mahi; A. R. Khan
method: Benchmark dataset release with MobileNet and DenseNet
main_contribution: High-resolution image dataset capturing real-world vendor formalin immersion
difference_from_our_proposal: Formulates detection strictly as closed-set supervised learning; does not evaluate OOD rejection

title: An extensive dataset for successful recognition of fresh and rotten fruits
authors: N. Sultana; M. Jahan; M. S. Uddin
method: Multi-class CNN evaluation on 8 fruit varieties
main_contribution: Broad multi-species benchmark for fresh vs rotten classification
difference_from_our_proposal: Purely closed-set organic decay; does not contain chemical adulterants or OSR evaluation protocols

title: Internal fruit quality evaluation and out-of-distribution rejection via Gaussian process uncertainty
authors: H. Li; B. Zhang; X. Chen; Y. Liu
method: Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) epistemic variance thresholding
main_contribution: Introduced uncertainty-guided OOD rejection for non-destructive spectroscopy
difference_from_our_proposal: Relies on expensive NIR/spectroscopy sensors rather than standard RGB packaging-line vision; continuous Brix/DM focus
